_meta.task: Empirically determine British .sbs → 2048² atlas pixel conversion
_meta.verdict: DEFINITIVE NEGATIVE — no uniform .sbs formula exists
_meta.formula_negative_reason: The .sbs per-vehicle Transformation2D offset values encode decal positions in each vehicle's own UV space, but the per-vehicle scale factor (SD units → atlas pixels) varies by vehicle: sexton≈233, sherman_firefly≈35, cromwell impossible (GT position geometrically unreachable by any available .sbs decal). No single formula {cx=(0.5+u/scale)*2048, cy=(0.5±v/scale)*2048} works across vehicles.

formula_details.sexton: scale=233, flip_v=false, decal=british_crest_02 → (1247,1081) within 6px of scan GT (1245,1087)
formula_details.sherman_firefly: scale=35, flip_v=false, decal=british_crest_03 → (206,490) within 29px of wikinger GT (185,510)
formula_details.cromwell: NO MATCH — cromwell GT (1740,1490) requires u_norm=+0.350, but british_decal_heavy_01 at scale=25 produces V out of atlas range. Geometrically impossible.

_meta.method: Decoded RGT textures from ArtBritish.sga and Wikinger community SGA (1418203330.sga) using fixed CoH2 RGT parser (28-byte chunk header with 8-byte GUID). Scanned 13 stock skin variants per vehicle for bright connected components (lum>100). Cross-checked .sbs transform offsets against scan-derived centers.
_meta.rgt_parser_fix: CoH2 RGT uses 28-byte chunk header (20 std + 8-byte GUID), NOT the 20-byte header assumed by scan.py. Fix: payload_off = off + 28 + name_len. Without this fix all British vehicles returned 'No mip data found'.
_meta.wikinger_sga: 1418203330.sga contains: cromwell, sherman_firefly, comet, sexton, churchill summer/winter variants

cromwell.note: Wikinger skin (4a167bb423654fd6be7a0d8c6b7f9f25) shows prominent white Allied 5-pointed star at this location. High confidence, ±30px. Pre-existing authored GT rect — unchanged.
cromwell.sbs_note: No cromwell .sbs decal maps to this position at any scale. GT position unreachable.

sherman_firefly.note: Wikinger skin shows white Allied star at upper-left atlas region. High confidence, ±30px. Pre-existing authored GT rect — unchanged.
sherman_firefly.sbs_note: british_crest_03 at per-vehicle scale=35, flip_v=false → (206,490), 29px from GT center. Per-vehicle scale (35) differs from sexton (233) confirming no uniform formula.

sexton.note: 8/13 stock skin variants (british_0001..0004, 0007, 0011 summer) show bright circular marking (white roundel with cross) at atlas (1245,1087), bbox 37x33. Markings in skins 0009/0010/0012/0013 are large custom paint areas that overshadow this location. .sbs british_crest_02 at scale=233, no-flip independently maps to (1247,1081) — 6px from scan center — providing cross-validation.
sexton.sbs_note: british_crest_02 at per-vehicle scale=233, flip_v=false → (1247,1081) within 6px. Scale=233 is sexton-specific.

comet.note: Stock skin scan: 11/13 skins found markings but with very high variance (centers scattered from (174,220) to (2006,1434), median (1650,996)). Wikinger skin shows yellow tactical number box at (634,1723). No consistent hull-side UV region identifiable from bright-pixel scanning. Faction fallback used.
comet.sbs_note: Comet .sbs transforms not tested against scan GT (no reliable GT). Scale factor unknown.

churchill.note: Stock skin scan: skins 0001-0004 consistently show markings near (1619-1627, 1892) at lower-right area. However median across all 9 found skins is (1065,1892) with high variance. Wikinger skin shows heraldic shield at (636,1470). Churchill UV atlas is also used by tanksurface.sbs (shared decal layer). Low confidence — faction fallback retained.
churchill.sbs_note: Churchill .sbs IS the tanksurface (same graph). Decal positions are in Churchill UV space (confirmed).

comet_scan_low._note: ALTERNATIVE for comet if operator wants to use Wikinger-derived position rather than fallback
comet_scan_low.note: Wikinger skin comet shows bright yellow tactical number box at (634,1723). This IS in the hull-side UV region (lower-left area of atlas) but represents a TACTICAL NUMBER, not an Allied star. Low confidence as hull-side decal placement anchor — only usable if decal should be placed at this specific tactical number location.
